page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture, powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7H12 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. It provides 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs via multithreading, paired with 128 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Cache features include 16 MB of L3 cache alongside standard hardware acceleration instructions including AVX, AES, and SHA_NI. The instance relies entirely on network-attached storage as local disk space is not included, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 16 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong multi-threaded compute and instruction performance, highlighted by top 25% scores in the Passmark CPU score, Passmark extended instructions, Passmark encryption, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 251.92 GB/sec. Geekbench ray tracing performance is also strong. However, single-core efficiency is a notable tradeoff, with stress-ng single-core performance falling into the bottom 10% and single-threaded gzip compression landing in the bottom 25%. Multi-core Geekbench, software compilation, static web serving, and memory bandwidth tests show average performance.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high vCPU count relative to memory makes this instance economical for heavily parallelized, compute-intensive tasks where single-thread clock latency is secondary. Given the 16 Gbps baseline network throughput and reliance on remote storage, it delivers high resource density for multi-threaded batch processing, software compilation, cryptography operations, and parallel web microservices, while being less suited for single-threaded jobs or memory-heavy databases.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance equipped with a 32-core, 64-vCPU AMD EPYC 7H12 processor clocked at 2.6 GHz and 128 GB of RAM. Featuring a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 2.0 GB per vCPU, it delivers core density without local storage, relying on network storage coupled with a 16 Gbps network bandwidth baseline. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate strong multi-core performance, extended instruction execution, encryption capability, and ray tracing execution, placing in the top 25% across several multi-threaded Passmark tests and bzip3 decompression. Single-core performance presents a tradeoff, scoring in the lower tier for single-threaded stress-ng and compression workloads. Multi-core compiling, memory bandwidth, and static web serving yield average results. The hardware profile offers parallel compute density, making it suitable for concurrent workloads such as parallel batch processing, software compilation, encryption services, and high-concurrency microservices.
